title: 〜ままに
meaning: just as …; at the mercy of …; following (one's heart, feet, orders)
simpleExplanation: 〜ままに means letting something else decide your action: 言われるままに署名した = "signed just as he was told"; 足の向くままに歩いた = "walked wherever my feet took me". まま is "the state as it is"; に turns it into "in accordance with". The subject is passive, following instructions, impulses, or a flow.
whenUsed: Written and literary Japanese, narratives and essays. Common with passive verbs (言われる・命じられる・誘われる), motion or feeling nouns (足の向く・心の赴く・気の向く), and 思いのままに / 欲望のままに. In casual speech people say 〜とおりに or 〜に任せて.
formation: V受身 + ままに  (言われるままに・命じられるままに)
Vる + ままに  (足の向くままに・心の赴くままに・気の向くままに)
N + の + ままに  (思いのままに・欲望のままに)
Set phrases: 思いのままに (as one wishes)・時の流れるままに

examples.ja: 彼は言われるままに、書類に署名した。
examples.reading: かれはいわれるままに、しょるいにしょめいした。
examples.en: He signed the documents just as he was told.
examples.note: Passive 言われる + ままに: he simply did as told.

examples.ja: 足の向くままに、知らない町を歩いた。
examples.reading: あしのむくままに、しらないまちをあるいた。
examples.en: I wandered through the unfamiliar town wherever my feet took me.
examples.note: 足の向く + ままに: wandering without a plan.

examples.ja: 彼は心の赴くままに絵を描いた。
examples.reading: かれはこころのおもむくままにえをかいた。
examples.en: He painted as his heart moved him.
examples.note: 心の赴く + ままに: painting as inspiration led.

examples.ja: 彼は上司に命じられるままに、不正な書類を作成してしまった。
examples.reading: かれはじょうしにめいじられるままに、ふせいなしょるいをさくせいしてしまった。
examples.en: Doing just as his boss ordered, he ended up preparing fraudulent documents.
examples.note: Passive + ままに with a critical tone.

examples.ja: 定年後は、気の向くままに旅をして暮らしたい。
examples.reading: ていねんごは、きのむくままにたびをしてくらしたい。
examples.en: After retirement, I want to live travelling wherever the mood takes me.
examples.note: 気の向くままに is a set phrase.

similarGrammar.difference: Everyday "just as (instructed)" (言われたとおりに). ままに is literary and adds a sense of passivity or drifting.
"In line with" a plan or policy, formal and neutral. ままに implies yielding control.
"In accordance with" instructions, or "as X changes". ままに stresses passivity or free drift more than compliance.

commonMistakes.right: 言われるままに署名した。
commonMistakes.why: When another person controls the action, the verb is passive (言われる).
In this set phrase the subject inside the modifier takes の, as is usual in literary style.

commonMistakes.wrong: （会話で）先生に言われるままに書いたよ。
commonMistakes.right: 先生に言われたとおりに書いたよ。
commonMistakes.why: ままに is literary; in casual speech use とおりに.

usageNotes: 思いのままに means "freely, at will" (思いのままに操る); ままに without の after 思い is not used.
The tone is often passive or drifting; with 命じられる it can criticize someone who did not think for themselves.
Literary narratives use 時の流れるままに ("as time flows") and 波のままに.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, a passive verb or a set phrase (足の向く・心の赴く・気の向く) + a blank is ままに.
Check the verb form: the passive is required when someone else directs the action.
In 並べ替え, ままに follows the modifier directly; the main action comes after.
